title: c equations in n variables with fibre dimension n-c at q: a principal localization is a relative global complete intersection
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $n,c\ge0$ integers, $f_1,\dots,f_c\in R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] and $S=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$. Let $\mathfrak q\subset S$ be a prime ideal, $\mathfrak p\subset R$ its inverse image, $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ the residue fields and $F=S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ the fibre ring [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]; let $\mathfrak Q\subset F$ be the kernel of the ring map $F\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$, $s\otimes\lambda\mapsto\bar s\bar\lambda$ (a prime ideal). Assume that the Krull dimension of the topological space $\operatorname{Spec}F$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] at the point $\mathfrak Q$ [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point] equals $n-c$. Then there is $h\in R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ whose image $g\in S$ satisfies $g\notin\mathfrak q$, such that $T=R[x_1,\dots,x_{n+1}]/(f_1,\dots,f_c,hx_{n+1}-1)$ (with $n+1$ variables and $c+1$ equations) is a relative global complete intersection [def-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection] and the $R$-algebra homomorphism $T\to S_g$, $x_i\mapsto(x_i\bmod(f))/1$ ($i\le n$), $x_{n+1}\mapsto1/g$, is an isomorphism of $R$-algebras, $S_g$ the localization of $S$ at $\{1,g,g^2,\dots\}$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00ST (lemma-localize-relative-complete-intersection, line 36671), part (3) and its proof (lines 36715-36720, via Lemma Tag 00QH lemma-dimension-fibres-bounded-open-upstairs, line 31308); dim_q(S/R) there is the dimension of Spec F at Q; tag verified in stacks-project/tags/tags (00ST,algebra-lemma-localize-relative-complete-intersection). The node lem-weil-pbc-equation-count-fibre-dimension-flat states the flatness consequence of the same part.

proof.text: (Setting; an open neighbourhood of $\mathfrak q$ with fibre dimension $\le n-c$.) Write $P=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], $\pi:P\to S$ the quotient map and $I=(f_1,\dots,f_c)$. Since $\pi$ is a surjective $R$-algebra homomorphism from a polynomial ring in finitely many variables, $R\to S$ is of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. For a prime $\mathfrak q'$ of $S$ write $\dim_{\mathfrak q'}(S/R)$ for the dimension at the point $\mathfrak Q'$ of the spectrum of the fibre ring as in [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-dimension-bounded-open-upstairs]; the hypothesis says $\dim_{\mathfrak q}(S/R)=n-c$ (in particular $n-c\ge0$, as the dimension of a space at a point is $\ge0$). By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-dimension-bounded-open-upstairs] with $d=n-c$ there is an open $V\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}S$ with $\mathfrak q\in V$ and $\dim_{\mathfrak q'}(S/R)\le n-c$ for all $\mathfrak q'\in V$. (Source: 'By Lemma 00QH there exists a $g\in S$, $g\notin\mathfrak q$ such that all nonempty fibres of $R\to S_g$ have dimension $\le n-c$'.)

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00ST (lemma-localize-relative-complete-intersection, line 36671), proof of (3), lines 36715-36720

proof.text: (Choice of $g$ and $h$.) By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open] (i) there is $g\in S$ with $\mathfrak q\in D(g)\subseteq V$, i.e. $g\notin\mathfrak q$ and every prime $\mathfrak q'$ of $S$ with $g\notin\mathfrak q'$ lies in $V$. As $\pi$ is surjective choose $h\in P$ with $\pi(h)=g$ (source: 'Let $h\in R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ be any element that maps to $g$').

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00ST (lemma-localize-relative-complete-intersection, line 36671), proof of (3), lines 36715-36720

proof.text: (The presentation: $T\cong S_g$.) Let $P'=R[x_1,\dots,x_{n+1}]=P[x_{n+1}]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-scalar-extension] (with $A=P$, the ring $S$, one variable $x_{n+1}$) $S\otimes_PP'\cong S[x_{n+1}]$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change] (with $A=P$, $B=P'$, the ideal $I$) $P'/IP'\cong P'\otimes_P(P/I)=P'\otimes_PS$; composing, the $R$-algebra map $\sigma:P'\to S[x_{n+1}]$ with $x_i\mapsto\pi(x_i)$ ($i\le n$), $x_{n+1}\mapsto x_{n+1}$ is surjective with kernel $IP'=(f_1,\dots,f_c)P'$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-away-polynomial-quotient] (ring $S$, $r=g$) the $S$-algebra map $\lambda:S[x_{n+1}]\to S_g$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away], $x_{n+1}\mapsto1/g$, is surjective with kernel $(gx_{n+1}-1)$. Hence $\lambda\sigma:P'\to S_g$ is a surjective $R$-algebra map with $x_i\mapsto(x_i\bmod(f))/1$, $x_{n+1}\mapsto1/g$, and since $\sigma(hx_{n+1}-1)=gx_{n+1}-1$ and $\sigma$ is surjective with kernel $IP'$, its kernel is $\sigma^{-1}\big((gx_{n+1}-1)S[x_{n+1}]\big)=(hx_{n+1}-1)P'+IP'=(f_1,\dots,f_c,hx_{n+1}-1)$. So $\lambda\sigma$ induces the $R$-algebra isomorphism $T=R[x_1,\dots,x_{n+1}]/(f_1,\dots,f_c,hx_{n+1}-1)\xrightarrow{\sim}S_g$ of the statement (source: '$S_g=R[x_1,\dots,x_n,x_{n+1}]/(f_1,\dots,f_c,hx_{n+1}-1)$'; the proof of 00SS (2): '$S_g\cong S[x_{n+1}]/(gx_{n+1}-1)$').

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00ST (line 36671), the displayed presentation of S_g; Lemma Tag 00SS (lemma-base-change-relative-global-complete-intersection, line 36640), proof of (2), line 36665

proof.text: (Every point of every fibre of $S$ has local dimension $\ge n-c$.) Let $\mathfrak p'\subset R$ be a prime, $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ and $F'=S\otimes_Rk$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-scalar-extension] $P\otimes_Rk\cong k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$, and by associativity of $\otimes$ and [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change] (with $A=P$, $B=k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$) $F'=(P/I)\otimes_Rk\cong\bar F':=k[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(\bar f_1,\dots,\bar f_c)$, $\bar f_j$ the image of $f_j$ under the coefficient map $R\to k$. The ring $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] (a field is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]: its only ideals are $0$ and $k$). Let $\bar{\mathfrak Q}$ be a prime of $\bar F'$ and $\tilde{\mathfrak Q}\supseteq(\bar f_1,\dots,\bar f_c)$ its inverse image in $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-quotient-dimension-at-point-height-difference] the heights $\operatorname{ht}\bar{\mathfrak Q}\le\operatorname{ht}\tilde{\mathfrak Q}\le n$ are integers and $\dim_{\bar{\mathfrak Q}}\operatorname{Spec}\bar F'=n-\operatorname{ht}\tilde{\mathfrak Q}+\operatorname{ht}\bar{\mathfrak Q}$; by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-height-quotient-bound] (with $t=c$, $J=(\bar f_1,\dots,\bar f_c)$) $\operatorname{ht}\tilde{\mathfrak Q}\le\operatorname{ht}\bar{\mathfrak Q}+c$. Hence $\dim_{\bar{\mathfrak Q}}\operatorname{Spec}\bar F'\ge n-c$. Isomorphic rings have homeomorphic spectra and a homeomorphism preserves the dimension at a point [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point], so $\dim_{\mathfrak Q}\operatorname{Spec}F'\ge n-c$ for every prime $\mathfrak Q$ of $F'$. (The source leaves this lower bound implicit; it is the count 'dim $\ge n-c$ by Lemma 00KW applied $c$ times' of the paragraph after Definition 00S9, line 35841.)

source.place: Algebra, the paragraph after Definition Tag 00S9 (definition-lci-field, lines 35834-35849: dim >= n - c by Lemma 00KW), with Lemma Tag 00P2 (lemma-codimension) as packaged in the cited height-difference node; used implicitly in the proof of Lemma Tag 00ST (3), lines 36715-36720

proof.text: (The fibres of $T$ are localizations of the fibres of $S$.) Keep $\mathfrak p'$, $k$, $F'$ and let $\bar g=g\otimes1\in F'$. The $R$-algebra isomorphism $T\cong S_g$ of step 3 gives $T\otimes_Rk\cong S_g\otimes_Rk$. Since $S_g\otimes_Rk\cong S_g\otimes_S(S\otimes_Rk)=S_g\otimes_SF'$ (associativity of $\otimes$) and, by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-away-tensor-iso] (with $A=S$, $M=F'$, $f=g$), $F'\otimes_SS_g\cong F'_g$, $m\otimes(s/g^e)\mapsto sm/g^e$, where the localization of the $S$-module $F'$ at $g$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away] is the ring $F'_{\bar g}$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away] since $g$ acts on $F'$ as multiplication by $\bar g$, and this map is multiplicative, we get a ring isomorphism $T\otimes_Rk\cong F'_{\bar g}$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00ST (3), proof line 36717 ('all nonempty fibres of $R\to S_g$'): the fibre of $R\to S_g$ over a prime is the localization of the fibre of $R\to S$

proof.text: (Every point of every fibre of $T$ has local dimension exactly $n-c$.) Let $X=\operatorname{Spec}(T\otimes_Rk)$ and $Y=\operatorname{Spec}F'$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. By step 5 $X$ is homeomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}F'_{\bar g}$, which by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open] (ii) maps homeomorphically onto the open subset $D(\bar g)\subseteq Y$ by $\mathfrak P\mapsto$ its inverse image in $F'$. Let $x\in X$ and $y=\mathfrak Q''\in D(\bar g)$ its image. Then $\dim_xX=\dim_y D(\bar g)$ (a homeomorphism preserves the dimension at a point [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point]) $=\dim_yY$ by [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-open-subspace]. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection] (with $A=R$, $B=S$, $C=F'$, $j:S\to F'$) $\mathfrak q''=j^{-1}(\mathfrak Q'')$ is a prime of $S$ lying over $\mathfrak p'$ and $\mathfrak Q''=\ker\psi_{\mathfrak q''}$ is the kernel of $F'\to\kappa(\mathfrak q'')$, so $\dim_yY=\dim_{\mathfrak q''}(S/R)$ in the notation of step 1; and $g\notin\mathfrak q''$ since $j(g)=\bar g\notin\mathfrak Q''$. By step 2 $\mathfrak q''\in V$, so $\dim_yY\le n-c$ by step 1, and $\dim_yY\ge n-c$ by step 4. Hence $\dim_xX=n-c$ for every $x\in X$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00ST (lemma-localize-relative-complete-intersection, line 36671), proof of (3), lines 36715-36720

proof.text:
(Conclusion.) Let $\mathfrak p'\subset R$ be a prime with $T\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p')
eq0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-prime-in-image-iff-fibre-ring-nonzero] there is a prime of $T$ over $\mathfrak p'$, hence by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection] a prime of $T\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p')$, so $X
eq\emptyset$. By [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-supremum-local-dimensions] and step 6, $\dim X=\sup_{x\in X}\dim_xX=n-c=(n+1)-(c+1)$. So every nonempty fibre of $\operatorname{Spec}T	o\operatorname{Spec}R$ has dimension $(n+1)-(c+1)$, i.e. $T=R[x_1,\dots,x_{n+1}]/(f_1,\dots,f_c,hx_{n+1}-1)$ is a relative global complete intersection [def-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection]. With step 2 ($g=\pi(h)
otin\mathfrak q$) and step 3 ($T\cong S_g$ by the stated map) this is the statement.

split_report.summary: Checked against Stacks 00ST (3) and its proof (lines 36715-36720). The source cites 'Lemma 00RJ' in the brief/node place, but tag 00RJ is algebra-lemma-extend-field-CM-locus; the lemma used, lemma-dimension-fibres-bounded-open-upstairs, is tag 00QH (corrected in source.place). Seven steps: (1) 00QH gives an open V around q where the fibre dimension at points is <= n-c (new unsplit node lem-weil-pbc-fibre-dimension-bounded-open-upstairs); (2) a basic open D(g) inside V, h a preimage of g (new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open, basic opens basis and Spec A_f = D(f)); (3) T = R[x_1..x_{n+1}]/(f, hx_{n+1}-1) is isomorphic to S_g, from the polynomial/tensor/localization leaves (the existing 00SS (2) node lem-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection-principal-localization cannot be used: it assumes S itself is a relative global complete intersection); (4) the lower bound n-c at every point of every fibre of S, written out (implicit in the source) from the height-difference node and Krull's height bound; (5) the fibre of T is the localization of the fibre of S at g; (6) so every point of a fibre of T has local dimension exactly n-c (open subspace, fibre-prime bijection); (7) dimension = sup of local dimensions (0B7I) gives dimension (n+1)-(c+1) for every nonempty fibre. Statement unchanged; checked against the citer's step 10.

lean.statement: theorem exists_localization_relativeGlobalCompleteIntersection (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (n c : ℕ) (f : Fin c → MvPolynomial (Fin n) R) (q : PrimeSpectrum (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range f))) (hdim : let S := MvPolynomial (Fin n) R ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range f) let p := PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap R S) q c ≤ n ∧ topologicalKrullDimAt (PrimeSpectrum.preimageEquivFiber R S p ⟨q, rfl⟩) = (n - c : ℕ)) : ∃ h : MvPolynomial (Fin n) R, let S := MvPolynomial (Fin n) R ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range f) let g : S := Ideal.Quotient.mk _ h g ∉ q.asIdeal ∧ let relations : Option (Fin c) → MvPolynomial (Option (Fin n)) R := Option.elim' (MvPolynomial.rename some h * MvPolynomial.X none - 1) (fun i ↦ MvPolynomial.rename some (f i)) let T := MvPolynomial (Option (Fin n)) R ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range relations) IsRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection (algebraMap R T) ∧ (∀ (p : Ideal R) (_hp : p.IsPrime), letI : p.IsPrime := _hp Nontrivial (p.Fiber T) → c + 1 ≤ n + 1 ∧ topologicalKrullDim (PrimeSpectrum (p.Fiber T)) = (n + 1 - (c + 1) : ℕ)) ∧ ∃ e : T ≃ₐ[R] Localization.Away g, (∀ i : Fin n, e (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (MvPolynomial.X (some i))) = algebraMap S (Localization.Away g) (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (MvPolynomial.X i))) ∧ e (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (MvPolynomial.X none)) = IsLocalization.Away.invSelf g
